subsystems.name: Solar power
subsystems.role: supplies electricity where sunlight is 25 times weaker than at Earth.
parts: two cross-shaped solar arrays covering about 85 m²
rechargeable batteries for eclipses and high-power manoeuvres

subsystems.name: Propulsion and attitude control
subsystems.role: flies the long cruise, inserts into Jupiter orbit and aims the instruments.

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: keeps fuel lines, mechanisms and electronics within limits from near-Venus to cold Jupiter.

subsystems.name: Telecommunications and data
subsystems.role: sends science data hundreds of millions of kilometres to Earth.

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: remote sensing, radar sounding, fields and particles, and radio science.

buildSteps.title: Design around Jupiter's radiation
buildSteps.detail: A tour that dips near Europa and Callisto accumulates a large radiation dose, so electronics are shielded, components are rad-hard, and the orbit is shaped to limit exposure.

buildSteps.title: Build the solar arrays
buildSteps.detail: Cells are laid on large lightweight panels and hinged to fold for launch; they must still make useful power at Jupiter.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the instruments
buildSteps.detail: Each instrument is built and calibrated separately, including a 16 m radar antenna and a long magnetometer boom that must deploy reliably and not disturb the magnetic field it measures.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Instruments, tanks, avionics and the dish are integrated onto the central structure and the deployable appendages are fitted.

buildSteps.title: Test on the ground
buildSteps.detail: Thermal-vacuum, vibration, acoustic and electromagnetic-compatibility tests reproduce launch and space conditions before shipping to the launch site.

buildSteps.title: Launch and commission
buildSteps.detail: It left Earth in 2023 and spent its first months unfolding arrays, booms and antennas and checking every instrument.

buildSteps.title: Cruise with gravity assists
buildSteps.detail: Flybys of the Moon and Earth, then Venus and Earth again, bend the trajectory outward — no rocket carries enough fuel to reach Jupiter directly with this payload.

buildSteps.title: Jupiter orbit insertion and tour
buildSteps.detail: On arrival the engine slows the craft into a long, looping Jovian orbit, then a sequence of Callisto and Europa flybys trades altitude for the right conditions.

buildSteps.title: Enter Ganymede orbit
buildSteps.detail: The tour ends by lowering the orbit until the spacecraft circles Ganymede itself — the first time a spacecraft has orbited a moon other than our own.

prerequisites.why: the mission reaches Jupiter only by stealing orbital energy from Venus and Earth.
Jupiter's belts would otherwise disable the computers within hours.

prerequisites.tech: Large-area solar arrays for the outer Solar System
prerequisites.why: solar power at Jupiter requires enormous panel area instead of a nuclear source.
radar sounding has worked at Mars, but sounding kilometres of ice at Ganymede and Europa is a harder, less proven task.
large ground antennas are needed to receive the very weak signal from Jupiter.

pathway.milestone: cruise with a lunar–Earth flyby in 2024 and a Venus flyby in 2025
pathway.unlocks: testing instruments and navigation in real planetary encounters.

pathway.milestone: Earth flybys that place the craft on a Jupiter-bound path, arriving in 2031
pathway.unlocks: entry into the Jovian system with enough propellant left to tour.

pathway.milestone: Callisto and Europa flybys, then orbit around Ganymede from 2034
pathway.unlocks: direct measurement of a subsurface ocean's depth and setting under an icy shell.

pathway.milestone: results combined with other Jovian missions and any future lander
pathway.unlocks: a basis for judging whether icy moons could support life.
